_readme: 2026-11-11 INDEX HAUPTMENÜ: additive fields read by js/index-hauptmenu.js — `menu_focus` (CSS object-position of the identity image inside the PORTRAIT 9:16 card — cards are portrait at every breakpoint, never landscape), `menu_order` (canonical monument order in the main menu: 1 Steinerne, 2 Dom, 3 Porta Praetoria, 4 Altes Rathaus, 5 Neupfarrplatz; the older `order` still drives js/gallery.js) and `menu_timeline` (null = no timeline yet -> compact "in preparation" card; else { src, poster, base:"assets_root"|"web_root", duration_s, burned_text, chapters:null|{ times[], labels_module, labels_key } }). The timeline `src` MUST point at the runtime file the monument page already uses — never a copy. A monument becomes active in the menu when enabled=true + route + menu_timeline are set. 2026-10-09 INTERACTIVE ROUTE TRAILER: optional `interactive_route` {media_type:"trailer", trailer_src, poster_src, base:"assets_root"|"web_root"|"" , aspect_ratio, preload, autoplay, muted, loop, playsinline}; null/absent = static poster fallback (index cards stay static posters via video_mode). Resolved by js/gallery.js through zt-paths.js (MASTER vs deploy safe). ZEITSPRUNG V2 — MAIN INDEX monument gallery config (Phase 2.7, extended Phase 2.7C.2). Single source of truth read by js/gallery.js. Fields: id, order, name{de,en,es}, subtitle{de,en,es}, description{de,en,es}, visual, poster, status(active|in_development), enabled(bool), route(relative path from ZEITSPRUNG_V2/index.html, or null), cta{de,en,es} (label shown on the action affordance; for non-enabled monuments this is a status badge, not a link), languages. Image paths are relative to ZEITSPRUNG_V2/ (this file's own folder), mirroring how `route` is also resolved relative to index.html — a deliberate, documented choice distinct from STEINERNE_BRUECKE/js/main.js's own internal absolute-from-server-root WEB_ASSET_BASE convention (that convention is scoped to files living one level deeper, under STEINERNE_BRUECKE/js/). Adding monument #6+ in the future = appending one object here; no HTML/JS template changes required as long as it reuses this same field set. PHASE 2.7C.2 additive fields: `video` (relative path to the primary clip, or null — muted/playsinline/no controls, only plays while this monument is the active one), `video_reverse` (relative path to a companion clip that continues the SAME transformation in reverse, or null — when present, gallery.js chains video<->video_reverse on `ended` for a true ping-pong assembly/disassembly loop instead of a native single-file loop; today only steinerne-bruecke has this), `video_mode` (`assembly_loop` = structural transformation content, native loop=true unless video_reverse is present, in which case it is the ping-pong pair described above | `ambient_loop` = single self-contained reveal clip, native loop=true | `static` = no video, still image only), `poster` now doubles as the `<video poster>` for whichever monument has a `video` (kept equal to `visual` when no dedicated frame grab exists), `background` (path used for the blurred full-bleed backdrop layer — video path when a video exists so the backdrop plays the same clip blurred, else the same value as `visual`; never a separate/different asset, see gallery.js applyBg()). PHASE 2.7C.4 — final index media reconnection: dom-st-peter/altes-rathaus/porta-praetoria/neupfarrplatz now point `video`/`poster`/`background` at the new monument-specific derivatives under `assets/video/index/monument_presentation/<id>/card_loop_01_web.mp4` (+ `card_poster_01.jpg`), all audio-stripped/+faststart web copies of 03_ASSETS/VIDEO/INDEX/MONUMENT_PRESENTATION masters. neupfarrplatz is the ONE exception to the `visual`-stays-a-curated-hero-shot rule noted above: it has no separate curated hero PNG, so `visual` is set equal to the new `poster` (not just `poster` alone) — gallery.js's tab-thumbnail empty-state check (`renderTabs()`) keys off `visual` specifically, so leaving `visual: null` would still render this monument's tab as the empty/placeholder swatch even with a real video wired. steinerne-bruecke's `video`/`video_reverse` pair (the bespoke pier/arch assembly<->disassembly transformation) was deliberately NOT replaced by the new `assets/video/index/monument_presentation/steinerne_bruecke/card_loop_01_web.mp4` file — that new file is a generic materials-cube presentation loop (same template as the other 4 monuments' new clips), not a bridge-specific structural transformation, and is judged lower-value than the already-working bespoke pair for this specific monument; the new file stays on disk, unreferenced, for a possible future Bau&Materialien use. dom-st-peter/altes-rathaus's PRIOR `*_gallery_loop_01_web.mp4` files (Phase 2.7C.2B, GLOBAL_INBOX-derived) remain on disk untouched (LEGACY_REFERENCE_ONLY, superseded by the MASTER-derived MONUMENT_PRESENTATION files). PHASE 3.0B — `01_ARCHITECTURE/scripts/zeitsprung-health.py`'s new Case Sensitivity check found dom-st-peter/altes-rathaus/porta-praetoria/neupfarrplatz's `video`/`poster`/`visual`/`background` paths pointing at lowercase `assets/video/index/monument_presentation/...` while the on-disk folder was then named `assets/VIDEO/` (uppercase) — an ALREADY-EXISTING mismatch (these fields were written this way back in Phase 2.7C.4, unrelated to anything Phase 3.0B did), working only because macOS's filesystem is case-insensitive. An initial Phase 3.0B pass fixed this by repointing these 4 monuments' fields at the uppercase folder — WRONG DIRECTION: `js/index-main.js`'s own already-live, working intro/vision-mission-objective code (and this file's own original lowercase fields) had already established lowercase `assets/video/index/...` as the one real WEB-runtime convention; repointing config at the accidentally-uppercase folder would have left that established convention permanently inconsistent instead of fixed. PHASE 3.0B-R — reconciled correctly: the on-disk folder itself was case-renamed `VIDEO` → `video` (a WEB-RUNTIME-layer rename, not a MASTER path, not git-tracked — `*.mp4`/`*.jpg` are gitignored) to match the established lowercase convention, and these 4 monuments' fields were reverted back to lowercase to match both `index-main.js` and their own original Phase 2.7C.4 values. See `PLATFORM_ARCHITECTURE_V3.md` Section E.1 for the full reconciliation. VIDEO DECODE PERFORMANCE HOTFIX — confirmed runtime diagnostic (repeated A/B/C/D toggle tests) found the gallery's blurred `background` layer was decoding a SECOND independent video stream of the exact same file as `video`, roughly doubling per-frame decode cost versus pausing/hiding it (measured ~33ms/frame with two streams vs ~16.6ms with one). First attempted fix (lightweight 360x640 `*_bg_web.mp4` derivatives per monument) FAILED its own local performance gate — re-measured at ~32ms/frame, essentially unchanged, proving the cost was tied to having a SECOND PLAYING VIDEO ELEMENT at all, not its resolution/bitrate. Those derivative files were generated (03_ASSETS + WEB copies) but never wired into `background`/`background_reverse` for this reason, and remain on disk unreferenced pending an explicit future decision. CANVAS MIRROR (current architecture) — `background`/`background_reverse` fields are consequently UNUSED again: js/gallery.js now draws the blurred backdrop from the SAME single authoritative `panelVideo` element via a throttled `<canvas>` mirror (see gallery.js's canvas draw loop), so there is no second decoder and no second source file to resolve at all. Fields kept at their pre-hotfix value (same file as `video`/`video_reverse`) only for schema stability / possible future reuse, not because anything currently reads them for the background layer. CONTENT POLISH 01 (2026-09-10) — steinerne-bruecke's `poster` field changed from the static hero PNG (assets/steinerne-bruecke/hero/sb_hero_current_9x16_v01.png, still used unchanged for `visual`/tab thumbnails and for STEINERNE_BRUECKE/js/main.js's own #stage "today-open" state) to a frame grab taken directly from the already-approved `video` asset itself (bridge_overview_card_poster_01.jpg, extracted from bridge_overview_assembly_v02_web.mp4 at t=2s) — the static hero photo was staying visibly layered under/instead of the video on the big INDEX card (see js/gallery.js's playClip()/reveal() fix in the same task), so the card's own fallback image needed to be a frame OF the same video, not an unrelated static hero shot.
